subject: Re: ggplot2 colors change brightness levels when saved in PDF

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 colors change brightness levels when saved in PDF
parts:
On 10/3/2012 11:10 AM, Ilya wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I'm creating report at work using ggplot2. On first page i put company
> logo/text and when i do that, and save everything in PDF colors on
> following changes loose intensity. Same green color on one page will be
> bright on on next dark. This is example of the code that will produces this
> bug on my machine. Colors on second and third pages (problems.pdf) will
> look different. Any suggesting on fixing it?
>
> Thank you
>
> library(ggplot2)
> library(scales)
> library(png)
> library(grid)
>
> data.set <-
> data.frame(year = c(2010, 2010, 2011,2011, 2012, 2012),
> overtime = c('TRUE', 'FALSE', 'TRUE', 'FALSE', 'TRUE', 'FALSE'),
> value = c(100, 200, 150, 250, 50, 75))
>
> logo <- readPNG(system.file("img", "Rlogo.png", package="png"))
> logo <- rasterGrob(logo, interpolate=TRUE)
> title.page <-
> qplot(1:10,1:10, geom = 'blank') +
> annotation_custom(logo, xmin = 0, xmax = 10, ymin = 8, ymax = 10)
>
>
> my.chart.1 <-
> ggplot(data = data.set,
> aes(x = overtime,
> y = value,
> fill = overtime)) +
> geom_bar(stat="identity")+
> scale_fill_manual(values = c('green','red'))
>
> my.chart.2 <-
> my.chart.1 +
> facet_wrap(~year)
>
> ## NO PROBLEMS
> pdf(file='no.problems.pdf')
> print(my.chart.1)
> print(my.chart.2)
> dev.off()
> ## PROBLEMS WITH COLORS
> pdf(file='problems.pdf')
> title.page
> print(my.chart.1)
> print(my.chart.2)
> dev.off()
>

I see this behavior as well (R version 2.15.1 (2012-06-22), Platform:
x86_64-pc-mingw32/x64 (64-bit), Adobe Reader version 10.1.4). I don't
know what is causing it, but I might have a workaround and some
additional information.

First, I see the different intensities problem even with pages shuffled:

pdf(file='problems2.pdf')
print(my.chart.1)
print(my.chart.2)
title.page
dev.off()

It's the inclusion of title.page, anywhere, that is the problem
(repeating my.chart.1 and my.chart.2 doesn't cause it).

I tried to dive into the PDF's themselves and see what the differences
were, but the compression made it incomprehensible. So I re-created the
PDF's without compression.

pdf(file="problems.pdf", compress=FALSE)
...

With this, the colors in "problems.pdf" were darker than in
"no.problems.pdf", but they were consistent! (Both graphs had a darker
green.) So this may be a workaround (though it will make bigger files,
obviously).

I looked at the (not compressed) PDF's and could not see any differences
that lept out at me as causing the differences (additional page graphic
and changes in the object numbers, but nothing related to color I noticed).

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

messages.author: 752cb0f8dd94a1e6
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 colors change brightness levels when saved in PDF
parts:
Thank you for your reply, Brian. 

Unfortunatly for some reason compress = FALSE didn't help. it was still producing variable colors, and compression is actually an issue, I would prefer to have files as small as possible - program will generate lots of reports. 

But thanks to your reply I started digging with pdf function and trying different options. 
All I want is consistency (to avoid confession and explaining why my colors are off for same measures on different charts). It looks like colormodel parameter did the trick. Default colormodel is "srgb", colormodel='cmyk' produced consistent colors (darker greens). It worked find in my example, I hope that it will work well in the report. 


ilya

PS in original post one might want to change title.page to print(title.page)
